body.intro: Every member's access is the combination of three independent choices:
body.portal: <term>1. Portal</term> decides which app they log into. Tenant portal users manage the organization; User portal users do day-to-day legal work.
body.role: <term>2. Role</term> decides what they can do there. Pick one or more roles that match the person's job.
body.region: <term>3. Region</term> decides which branch or jurisdiction data they see. The same person can have different roles in different regions.
body.example: Example: a Matter Manager in UAE and a portal user in Pakistan is one complete assignment. Change any choice from Members.

body.intro: A member belongs to exactly one of two internal portals, chosen when you invite them:
body.tenant: <term>Tenant portal</term> (admin) â€” manage members & invitations, roles, regions, departments, and view organization-wide oversight of contracts & litigation. This is where you are now.
body.user: <term>User portal</term> â€” the module workspace: create and work on contracts, litigation cases, compliance, and more, scoped to the member's region(s).
body.outro: The portal you pick decides which login the member uses and which <term>roles</term> are available to assign. (A third, platform-level <term>Super Admin</term> exists for the Tellara operators and isn't managed here.)

body.intro: <term>Permissions</term> are fine-grained capabilities such as "create contract" or "approve case fees". You never assign them one by one â€” instead you assign <term>roles</term>, which bundle related permissions for a job.
body.bullet1: A member can hold <term>more than one role</term>; their effective access is the <term>union</term> of all permissions across those roles.
body.bullet2: Tellara ships ready-made templates â€” e.g. <term>org_owner</term>, <term>org_admin</term>, <term>contract_manager</term>, <term>litigation_manager</term> â€” and you can create your own under <term>Roles</term>.
body.bullet3: Roles are tied to a portal: Tenant-portal roles grant admin abilities; User-portal roles grant module abilities.

body.intro: A region is a branch or jurisdiction of your organization (often a country, e.g. UAE, Pakistan). One region is your headquarters.
body.bullet1: Contracts, cases, departments, and members all belong to a region â€” switching the active region filters what you see.
body.bullet2: A person can be a member of several regions, with a different role in each. The organization owner works across all regions.
body.bullet3: Region is a data & access boundary â€” unlike a folder or department, it controls visibility.

body.intro: Departments mirror your internal structure as a hierarchy: Department â€º Sub-Department / Cost Center â€º Business / Function.
body.bullet1: When creating a contract or case you can tag it with a department â€” used for reporting and to route Matrix-of-Authority approvals to the right people.
body.bullet2: A department can have a Head of Department and a cost center / business function for finance grouping.
body.bullet3: Departments are organizational, not a security boundary â€” they don't decide who can see a record (region and roles do that).
body.outro: Optional but recommended â€” set them up under the Departments page.

body.intro: Folders are the labelled containers in the file-explorer view â€” a convenient way to group related cases or contracts (by matter, client, yearâ€¦ however you like).
body.bullet1: A record lives in exactly one folder, or none. Records with no folder appear under Unfiled on the Home view.
body.bullet2: Folders are purely organizational â€” they never change who can access a record, its region, or its approvals.
body.bullet3: Deleting a folder doesn't delete its records; they simply move back to Unfiled.
body.outro: Think of folders like folders on your computer, and departments like an org chart â€” different jobs.

body.intro: A <term>counterparty</term> is the external party on the other side of a contract (a vendor, client, partner). They're created once under <term>Compliance â†’ Counterparties</term> and then linked to any contract.
body.bullet1: <term>IDD</term> (Integrity Due Diligence / Anti-Bribery & Corruption) screens a counterparty against watch-lists (World-Check) and assigns a risk tier.
body.bullet2: If a contract has <term>"Require IDD clearance"</term> turned on, it <term>cannot be executed</term> until its linked counterparty has an approved IDD clearance.
body.bullet3: The contract form shows the counterparty's current clearance status so you know before you start.

body.intro: The Matrix of Authority decides who must approve a contract before it can be executed. You define rules once; the right chain is generated automatically per contract.
body.bullet1: A rule matches contracts by criteria â€” type, department, value range, and risk tier â€” and lists ordered approval steps (a specific person or a role, with an SLA).
body.bullet2: When a contract is submitted, the most specific matching rule builds its approval chain; each approver signs off in order.
body.bullet3: Configure rules under Contracts â†’ MoA Rules.

body.intro: <term>External counsel</term> are outside lawyers or consultants who need to see specific matters without being full members of your organization.
body.bullet1: You grant access through an <term>allocation</term> to a single case or contract, at <term>View</term> or <term>Contribute</term> level, optionally with an expiry.
body.bullet2: They sign into a dedicated, stripped-down <term>external portal</term> that shows only their allocated matters.
body.bullet3: Allocations are managed by Tenant admins; module users get a read-only directory of outside counsel engaged in their region.

body.intro: Your subscription includes two seat pools:
body.bullet1: <term>Admin seats</term> â€” consumed by members in the <term>Tenant portal</term>.
body.bullet2: <term>User seats</term> â€” consumed by members in the <term>User portal</term>.
body.outro: The badges on the Members page show <term>used / total</term>. Inviting someone reserves a seat of the portal you choose; if a pool is full, free one up (set a member to <term>Removed</term>) or contact your account manager to raise the limit.

body.intro: Integrations allow Tellara to connect directly with external services to automate workloads.
body.bullet1: <term>E-Signatures (DocuSign)</term> â€” automatically send finalized contracts to DocuSign for legally-binding signing, and track the status inside Tellara.
body.bullet2: <term>Counterparty Screening (World-Check)</term> â€” run automated IDD checks on your third parties against global sanctions, PEP, and enforcement lists.
body.bullet3: <term>Single Sign-On (SSO)</term> â€” allow members to log in securely using their existing Microsoft or Google work credentials.
